## global

Air-gapped and mirrored installs. imageRegistry replaces the registry host of every image this chart renders and keeps its repository path, the way `hauler store copy` names images: "ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:17" -&gt; "&lt;imageRegistry&gt;/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:17". The api also offers it as the default registry for managed vLLM images.

| Value                     | Default | Description         |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------- |
| `global.imageRegistry`    | `""`    |                     |
| `global.imagePullSecrets` | `[]`    | \[{name: regcred}\] |

## subprocess

runner: subprocess only. Secrets in the release namespace that RunSpecs name (target.auth, target.admin, an upstream key), each mounted read-only into the api pod at /etc/servtuner/secrets/&lt;name&gt;, where bench reads them. The Kubernetes runner mounts a run's Secrets into its Job itself and needs none of this. Names only; never put a value here.

| Value                | Default | Description              |
| -------------------- | ------- | ------------------------ |
| `subprocess.secrets` | `[]`    | for example \[vllm-key\] |

## ingress

Optional ingress-nginx routing (annotations are ingress-nginx's). Two Ingresses: the UI goes to the frontend under frontend.basePath, and ingress.apiPath (prefix stripped) goes to the api. Browser TLS is terminated here, outside servtuner. With TLS on the ingress -&gt; api connection the api Ingress uses backend TLS with the chart's ingress certificate Secret, which must carry ca.crt.

| Value                 | Default | Description                                                          |
| --------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ingress.enabled`     | `false` |                                                                      |
| `ingress.className`   | `""`    |                                                                      |
| `ingress.host`        | `""`    | required when enabled                                                |
| `ingress.apiPath`     | `""`    | empty = &lt;frontend.basePath&gt;/api; an explicit path is never "/" |
| `ingress.annotations` | `{}`    | added to both Ingresses                                              |

## gateway

Gateway API routing (ingress-nginx is retired): HTTPRoutes for the UI under frontend.basePath and the api under ingress.apiPath (prefix stripped), attached to a Gateway the cluster provides. Use this or `ingress`, not both. With TLS the gateway -&gt; api connection needs Envoy Gateway's Backend API (helm --set config.envoyGateway.extensionApis.enableBackend=true): a Backend carries the chart's ingress client certificate, and a BackendTLSPolicy verifies the api.

| Value                                    | Default                               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gateway.enabled`                        | `false`                               |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `gateway.parentRefs`                     | `[]`                                  | required: the Gateway(s), e.g. \[{name: eg, namespace: gateways}\]                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `gateway.hostname`                       | `""`                                  | required: the host the routes answer for                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `gateway.envoy`                          | section                               | Envoy Gateway extensions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `gateway.envoy.extAuth`                  | section                               | forward\_header through Envoy's external authorization: a SecurityPolicy on both routes asks this service, then copies headersToBackend onto the request, replacing any copy the client sent. A service in another namespace needs a ReferenceGrant there. |
| `gateway.envoy.extAuth.enabled`          | `false`                               |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `gateway.envoy.extAuth.service`          | `{"name":"","namespace":"","port":0}` |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `gateway.envoy.extAuth.path`             | `""`                                  | prefix for the auth request's path; empty keeps the request's                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `gateway.envoy.extAuth.headersToBackend` | `[]`                                  | empty: \[auth.forwardHeader.userHeader\]                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `gateway.envoy.extAuth.headersToExtAuth` | `[]`                                  | Client headers sent to the auth service. Empty keeps Envoy's default for HTTP services: only Host, Method, Path, Content-Length and Authorization; oauth2-proxy needs \[cookie\].                                                                          |

## auth

User auth. local checks every route; none checks nothing and is an explicit opt-out for installs whose ingress does all access control.

| Value                                  | Default              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auth.mode`                            | `"local"`            | local \| none                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `auth.methods`                         | `["local"]`          | any of local, forward\_header; the order is the order they are tried                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `auth.setupToken`                      | section              | The setup token creates the first admin, and only while there is none. Empty: the chart creates &lt;fullname&gt;-setup-token once and keeps it across upgrades (NOTES prints how to read it).                                                                                                 |
| `auth.setupToken.existingSecret`       | `""`                 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `auth.setupToken.key`                  | `"token"`            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `auth.session.idleTimeoutSeconds`      | `43200`              | 12 hours unused                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `auth.session.absoluteLifetimeSeconds` | `604800`             | 7 days after sign-in, whatever the use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `auth.cookie.secure`                   | `true`               | false only for a plain-HTTP install not on localhost                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `auth.lockout.maxFailures`             | `5`                  | failed logins per username                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `auth.lockout.windowSeconds`           | `900`                | the counting window and how long the lock lasts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `auth.forwardHeader`                   | section              | forward\_header: a proxy in front of the api (oauth2-proxy, an ingress auth-url, an ingress that verifies client certificates) names the user. The api trusts the header from whatever reaches it, so the proxy must overwrite any copy the client sends, and networkPolicy keeps others out. |
| `auth.forwardHeader.userHeader`        | `"X-Forwarded-User"` |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `auth.forwardHeader.displayNameHeader` | `""`                 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `auth.forwardHeader.emailHeader`       | `""`                 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `auth.forwardHeader.provisioning`      | `"refuse"`           | refuse \| viewer: what a subject with no servtuner user gets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## networkPolicy

NetworkPolicies: only the ingress controller and bench Jobs reach the api's port, and nothing reaches a bench pod. Egress is not restricted. They need a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy.

| Value                                               | Default                                                                  | Description                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `networkPolicy.enabled`                             | `true`                                                                   |                                                                                               |
| `networkPolicy.ingressController.namespaceSelector` | `{"matchLabels":{"kubernetes.io/metadata.name":"ingress-nginx"}}`        |                                                                                               |
| `networkPolicy.ingressController.podSelector`       | `{}`                                                                     | empty: any pod in those namespaces                                                            |
| `networkPolicy.gateway`                             | section                                                                  | With gateway.enabled: where the gateway's proxy pods run (Envoy Gateway's default namespace). |
| `networkPolicy.gateway.namespaceSelector`           | `{"matchLabels":{"kubernetes.io/metadata.name":"envoy-gateway-system"}}` |                                                                                               |
| `networkPolicy.gateway.podSelector`                 | `{}`                                                                     |                                                                                               |
| `networkPolicy.extraFrom`                           | `[]`                                                                     | more NetworkPolicyPeer entries allowed to reach the api's port                                |

## tuning

Managed targets: how Prometheus finds a managed vLLM. podmonitor needs the Prometheus Operator; scrape-annotations labels the pod servtuner.dev/scrape=true for the community chart's servtuner-targets job (deploy/prometheus/), which cannot verify a tls target, so tls needs podmonitor.

| Value            | Default        | Description |
| ---------------- | -------------- | ----------- |
| `tuning.monitor` | `"podmonitor"` |             |

## tls

Transport security: whether each connection uses TLS. Never inferred, never mixed on one connection. With TLS, each component presents its one certificate; the server decides whether to ask for it.

| Value                             | Default                                                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tls.enabled`                     | `true`                                                         | Whether connections use TLS; each connection can override it. false is plain HTTP or TCP: for a service mesh or an encrypted CNI that encrypts the connection, or for testing.                                                                                                         |
| `tls.clientAuth`                  | `"required"`                                                   | The api listener's client certificates (ingressApi, benchApi): required, optional (a certificate that is sent is verified, and tokens authenticate clients without one) or none.                                                                                                       |
| `tls.connections`                 | `{}`                                                           | Per-connection overrides, true or false; a connection not listed takes tls.enabled. The names: benchApi, benchPrometheus, ingressApi, objectStore, postgres. benchApi and ingressApi must agree (the api has one listener). Example: {postgres: false} (then postgres.auth password).  |
| `tls.source`                      | `"cert-manager"`                                               | cert-manager \| secret                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `tls.certManager.issuerRef`       | `{"kind":"ClusterIssuer","name":"","group":"cert-manager.io"}` |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tls.secrets`                     | section                                                        | source: secret. kubernetes.io/tls Secrets. The bench Secret must exist in the runs namespace. `objectStore` is the server certificate of the object store and is only validated here: the chart bundles no object store, and api/bench present their own api/bench certificates to it. |
| `tls.secrets.api`                 | `""`                                                           |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tls.secrets.bench`               | `""`                                                           |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tls.secrets.ingress`             | `""`                                                           |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tls.secrets.postgres`            | `""`                                                           |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tls.secrets.postgresReplication` | `""`                                                           | CNPG needs a streaming\_replica client certificate when it is given a client CA                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tls.secrets.objectStore`         | `""`                                                           |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tls.caSecretRef`                 | `null`                                                         | {name: &lt;secret with ca.crt&gt;} when the cert Secrets do not carry ca.crt                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `tls.caBundle.image`              | `{"repository":"","tag":""}`                                   | init container image; empty = the api image (has sh, cat and system CAs)                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `tls.caBundle.systemCaFile`       | `"/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt"`                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
